research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's guide: put the exact text in quotes and describe its lettering; for an edit, open with the verb, name the one thing that changes and say outright what must stay exactly the same; name a camera and film stock for the look (e.g. 'slightly grainy colour film', 'muted teal')
https://fal.ai/learn/tools/how-to-use-nano-banana-2 — quoted words with a stated position print cleanly; keep text short
https://www.atlabs.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-prompting-guide — 3-5 words at most for reliable rendering, so each card carries only a price
https://morphic.com/resources/how-to/nano-banana-2-lite-guide — targeted edits work as 'change only X, keeping the pose, framing and lighting unchanged'

https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/video/video-gen-prompt-guide — static shot means 'the camera remains completely still'; for image-to-video, describe the motion and change, not the picture again
https://ltx.studio/blog/veo-prompt-guide — Veo-class models drift into subtle handheld motion unless the camera is stated, so say tripod / locked in plain words

https://openpromptlib.pages.dev/prompt/thunder-strikes-silent-night-ride-W3lX_sdA — community Veo prompt: static tripod, no pan/tilt/roll/dolly, lightning as a light source from outside; a single sub-second flash reads as horror
notes: All three put a window or door glass inside the frame edge so the lightning has a source the model can see, and keep the outside dark so nothing is there to animate. The cards are flat white cards taped square onto a vertical front face (counter front, freezer front, window-ledge lip), one under each product with a clear gap between them, so they never touch or overlap a product and can be cut out as rectangles. The chocolate card is drawn wide (landscape) on purpose so '10p' crossed out plus '£12' still fits on it after the edit. Every prompt says the text stays the same and nothing moves, because text crawl in video is the most likely failure. No research source is about Omni 1.2 Flash specifically; the motion advice is from Veo-class guides and is unverified for Omni. The wrappers are described as plain purple with no print; the model may still invent a logo, so check before the edit. Choice of place: a = shop counter by the window, b = chest freezer lid by the front window, c = the front window ledge itself.

options.place: the shop counter, next to the front window
options.label: Counter by the dark window
options.still: Vertical candid photo, close shot of the end of a scuffed shop counter in a small British corner shop at night. A single loaf of plain white sliced bread in a clear plastic bag with a twisted end lies on the worn laminate counter top and fills the middle of the frame, close enough that it takes up nearly half the picture. Just to its right, with a clear gap of bare counter between them, lies one small chocolate bar in a plain purple wrapper with no logo, no words and no print on it at all. Behind them, the left edge of the frame is the shop's front window, black outside, a few raindrops on the glass, nothing visible beyond it. Two plain white price cards are taped flat and square onto the vertical front face of the counter, facing the camera straight on, not bent, not overlapping anything: a larger card directly under the loaf reading "£5", and a wide landscape card directly under the chocolate bar reading "10p", both written by hand in thick black marker. Lit only by a cold teal fluorescent tube overhead. Shot on cheap colour negative film at night, heavy grain, slightly soft focus, muted teal cast, deep shadows. No people, no hands, no shadows of people. Thanks.
options.edit: Change only the handwriting on the two white price cards taped to the front of the counter. On the card under the loaf, replace "£5" with "£50" in the same thick black marker handwriting. On the wide card under the purple chocolate bar, cross out "10p" with one straight black marker line and write "£12" beside it on the same card in the same handwriting. Keep everything else exactly the same: the bread, the chocolate bar, the counter, the window, the cards' size, position and shape, the framing, the light, the colour and the film grain. Thanks.
options.motion: Locked-off static shot on a tripod: the camera does not move at all, no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no shake. Nothing in the shop moves; the bread, the chocolate bar and the price cards stay perfectly still and the writing on the cards never changes. For the first two seconds the cold fluorescent light is steady. At about two seconds a single horror-film lightning flash bursts through the black window on the left, a hard white-blue light that blasts across the counter and the bread for a split second, flickers once more, and is gone. The light then returns to exactly the same steady fluorescent level as the start and holds, unchanged, to the end of the shot. Outside the window stays black. Low rumble of thunder, the hum of the fluorescent tube. No people, no voices. Thanks.
options.risk: Raindrops on the glass may tempt the model to animate rain running down the window, which changes the room after the flash; drop the raindrops if it does. The counter top could pick up clutter (till, lighter rack) that drifts.

options.place: lid of a chest freezer by the front door
options.label: Freezer lid by the door glass
options.still: Vertical candid photo, close shot of the white lid of an old chest freezer in a small British corner shop at night, the lid scratched and yellowed. A single loaf of plain white sliced bread in a clear plastic bag with a twisted end lies on the freezer lid and fills much of the frame, close and slightly from above. To its right, with a clear gap of bare lid between them, lies one small chocolate bar in a plain purple wrapper with no logo, no words and no print. In the top of the frame, behind the freezer, is the lower half of the shop's glass front door, black night outside, nothing visible through it. Two plain white price cards are taped flat and square onto the vertical white front side of the freezer, facing the camera straight on, not bent, not overlapping anything and well apart: a larger card directly below the loaf reading "£5", and a wide landscape card directly below the chocolate bar reading "10p", both handwritten in thick black marker. Cold teal fluorescent light from above, the freezer's own faint hum of a glow. Shot on cheap colour film at night, heavy grain, soft focus, muted teal-green cast, dark corners. No people, no hands, no shadows of people. Thanks.
options.edit: Change only the handwriting on the two white price cards taped to the front side of the freezer. On the card below the loaf, replace "£5" with "£50" in the same thick black marker handwriting. On the wide card below the purple chocolate bar, cross out "10p" with one straight black marker line and write "£12" beside it on the same card, same handwriting. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the bread, the chocolate bar, the freezer, the door glass, the cards' size, position and shape, the framing, the lighting, the colours and the grain. Thanks.
options.motion: Static camera locked on a tripod, completely still for the whole shot: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no drift. Nothing moves: the bread, the chocolate bar and the price cards stay exactly where they are, and the handwriting on the cards stays identical throughout. Steady cold fluorescent light for the first two seconds. At about two seconds, one sudden horror-style lightning flash explodes through the black glass of the door behind the freezer, a harsh blue-white burst that bleaches the freezer lid and the loaf for an instant, a second smaller flicker, then darkness outside again. The light settles back to exactly the same steady level as the opening and stays that way, unchanging, until the end. A crack of thunder, then only the freezer hum. No people, no voices. Thanks.
options.risk: A freezer front with a lid seam may push the cards to curl over an edge; check the cards are on a flat panel. The door glass may reflect the room and the model may 'reveal' something in the reflection on the flash; reject any take with a figure.

options.place: the inside ledge of the shop's front window
options.label: Window ledge, lightning outside
options.still: Vertical candid photo, close shot of the wide inside ledge of a corner shop's front window at night, a dusty painted wooden ledge with a few dead flies. A single loaf of plain white sliced bread in a clear plastic bag with a twisted end sits on the ledge, filling much of the frame. To its right, with a clear gap of bare ledge between them, lies one small chocolate bar in a plain purple wrapper with no logo, no words and no print. Directly behind them is the window glass, filling the upper part of the frame, pitch black outside with a faint smear of condensation, nothing visible through it. Two plain white price cards are taped flat and square onto the vertical front lip of the ledge, facing the camera straight on, not bent, not overlapping anything and well apart: a larger card directly under the loaf reading "£5", and a wide landscape card directly under the chocolate bar reading "10p", both handwritten in thick black marker. Lit from behind the camera by a cold teal fluorescent tube. Shot on cheap colour negative film at night, coarse grain, soft focus, muted teal cast, deep blacks. No people, no hands, no reflections of people. Thanks.
options.edit: Change only the handwriting on the two white price cards taped to the front lip of the window ledge. On the card under the loaf, replace "£5" with "£50" in the same thick black marker handwriting. On the wide card under the purple chocolate bar, cross out "10p" with a single straight black marker line and write "£12" beside it on the same card, in the same handwriting. Everything else stays exactly the same: the bread, the chocolate bar, the ledge, the black window, the cards' size, position and shape, the framing, the lighting, colour and grain. Thanks.
options.motion: Locked camera on a tripod, perfectly still, no movement of any kind: no pan, tilt, zoom or shake. Nothing in the frame moves; the loaf, the chocolate bar and the price cards stay still and the writing on the cards never changes. Steady fluorescent light for the first two seconds. At about two seconds, lightning strikes outside: the black window behind the bread blows out to a blinding blue-white for a split second, throwing the loaf into hard silhouette, then one shorter flicker, then black again. The light inside returns to exactly the same steady level as the opening and holds unchanged to the end. Thunder rolls, then silence and the faint buzz of the tube. Nothing appears outside the window. No people, no voices. Thanks.
options.risk: Highest scare but highest risk: with the whole window lit, the model may show a street, a tree or a shape outside on the flash, and the condensation may run. Backlit silhouette on the flash hides the cards, which is fine for the swap but check the flash frame is bright enough to hide the cut.
